claims.supporting_quote: The only study that has assessed homocysteine in cerebrospinal fluid reported that the concentration of this biomarker in migraine patients was significantly increased compared to controls.
Compared with controls, patients with migraine had higher levels of post-methionine load homocysteine values (19.5 +/- 4.9 vs. 16.9 +/- 1.9; P = 0.025)
Compared with women with no migraine history, women who reported any history of migraine had modestly increased adjusted odds ratios ... for ... homocysteine
Compared with controls, women with migraine had higher adjusted odds ratios for ... homocysteine
The homocysteine serum levels were significantly higher in migraine with aura compared to migraine without aura.

We found significant differences in homocysteine levels between various diagnostic groups (K-W test: p=0.005). One-way ANOVA, post-hoc tests revealed significant differences in homocysteine levels between Non-migraineurs, MWA (p=0.002, CI: 1.93 - 9.19) and MWoA (p=0.002, CI: -9.19 - -1.9).
plasma homocysteine levels were lower in MWA than in MWOA.
Meta-analysis was indicative of higher Hcy concentration in migraine patients vs HC overall [adults and children: 16 studies, I ...]
